skill.name: chapter-analyzer
skill.description: Validates Docusaurus MDX chapters for structure, teaching flow, required frontmatter, and supported interactive components.
skill.summary: Reviews Docusaurus MDX chapters for structure, pedagogy, component usage, and tone.
skill.author: AbdulSamad94

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and fenced YAML examples in SKILL.md. No shell execution, system reconnaissance, network access, prompt injection, or data exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed skill content.

static_findings.snippet: - Do not use H1 (`#`) within the body.
Every chapter must have valid YAML frontmatter:

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 9 uses Markdown inline code to name the textbook/docs/ directory. It does not invoke a shell or ask the assistant to execute external commands.
Line 10 uses Markdown inline code to show .mdx and .md file extensions. This is documentation text, not executable command syntax.
Line 14 opens a fenced YAML example for expected frontmatter. The fenced block documents metadata fields and contains no shell command or execution path.
Line 21 closes the YAML fenced block that began at line 14. It is Markdown formatting only and cannot execute commands.
Line 26 uses inline code to show Markdown heading syntax. It is a content rule for documents, not shell backtick execution.
Line 27 uses inline code to show the Markdown H1 marker. The text prohibits H1 usage in chapter bodies and does not run commands.
Line 37 uses inline code to display an MDX Quiz component example. It is a documented component pattern, not a command execution primitive.
Line 38 uses inline code to display an MDX Simulation component example. No command, subprocess, or shell expansion is requested.
Line 39 uses inline code to list MDX Tabs and TabItem components. The backticks are Markdown formatting around component names.
Line 13 introduces required YAML frontmatter for chapter files. It does not request host inspection, environment discovery, or system reconnaissance.
Lines 16 and 17 are sample frontmatter values for id and title. These are document metadata examples, not attempts to enumerate system information.
Line 44 is a tone guideline to avoid unexplained jargon. It has no relationship to system reconnaissance or sensitive data collection.

content.value_statement: Docusaurus chapters can drift from consistent structure and teaching quality. This skill reviews MDX chapters for frontmatter, flow, components, and tone.
actual_capabilities: Reviews MDX and Markdown chapters located under textbook/docs/.
Checks required YAML frontmatter fields for chapter metadata.
Validates heading hierarchy where the Docusaurus title acts as H1.
Assesses learning flow from introduction through summary.
Checks expected Quiz, Simulation, Tabs, and TabItem component usage.
Reviews tone for accessible explanations and clear terminology.
limitations: Does not include executable linting scripts or automated file traversal.
Assumes chapters follow the textbook/docs/ Docusaurus project layout.
Does not validate custom component props against a runtime schema.
Cannot verify simulations or diagrams without project-specific context.

use_cases.title: Review Course Chapters
use_cases.description: Check a draft lesson for required structure, learning objectives, interactive elements, and summary coverage.

use_cases.title: Standardize Documentation Quality
use_cases.description: Apply consistent chapter rules before publishing a Docusaurus documentation update.

use_cases.title: Improve Learning Experience
use_cases.description: Identify missing examples, unclear jargon, weak flow, or absent knowledge checks in educational content.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Chapter Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one draft chapter.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Docusaurus MDX chapter for structure, frontmatter, headings, and teaching flow. List the most important fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: Frontmatter And Headings Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this chapter against the expected frontmatter and heading hierarchy rules. Explain each issue and suggest corrected wording.

prompt_templates.title: Pedagogy And Component Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this chapter for learning objectives, examples, Quiz or Simulation placement, summaries, and accessible tone.

prompt_templates.title: Release Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across multiple chapter drafts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these Docusaurus chapter drafts for consistency, component coverage, teaching flow, tone, and publication readiness. Group findings by chapter.

output_examples.input: A draft MDX chapter with frontmatter, headings, and lesson content.
output: Frontmatter is present, but the sidebar label is missing.
The first body heading should start at H2 because the Docusaurus title acts as H1.
Add a Quiz after the core concept section to check understanding.

output_examples.input: A chapter that explains a ROS2 concept without interactive sections.
output: The introduction and objectives are clear.
The core content needs one Simulation or Quiz in each major section.
Several technical terms need short explanations for new learners.

output_examples.input: Several chapters prepared for a documentation release.
output: Chapter structure is mostly consistent across the set.
Two chapters need summaries that recap key points.
Tabs should be used where both Python and C++ examples are shown.

best_practices: Provide the full chapter text and any local component rules before review.
Ask for structure, pedagogy, and component feedback as separate review passes.
Request prioritized fixes so publishing blockers are addressed first.
anti_patterns: Reviewing only a small excerpt when frontmatter and flow matter.
Asking the skill to verify runtime behavior of custom components.
Treating suggestions as final without checking local style guidelines.

faq.question: What files does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Docusaurus MDX or Markdown chapters under textbook/docs/.

faq.question: Can it edit chapters directly?
faq.answer: It can suggest edits and revisions when used with an assistant that has file editing access.

faq.question: Does it run automated tests?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides review logic and does not include executable test scripts.

faq.question: What frontmatter does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects id, title, sidebar_label, and description fields in the chapter frontmatter.

faq.question: Which components does it recognize?
faq.answer: It references Quiz, Simulation, Tabs, and TabItem components for interactive chapter content.

faq.question: Is it suitable for non-educational docs?
faq.answer: It can help with structure, but its rules are designed for educational chapter content.
